name: Penken-Joch
kurzbeschreibung: Penkenjoch in the Zillertal impresses with the modern 3S Penkenbahn, Mario Botta's futuristic Granatkapelle, and watersports at the reservoir.
preis: Plateau freely accessible; Mayrhofen or Finkenberg mountain lifts chargeable
oeffnungszeiten: Open mid-May to late October and December to mid-April
beschreibung:
Overview

The vibrant and sun-drenched Penkenjoch perches at 2,095 meters above sea level high over the Zillertal, serving as the central hub of the Mayrhofen and Finkenberg mountain railways. Encircled by the glaciated summits of the Zillertal and Tux Alps, this high plateau blends sensational mountain scenery, modern recreational attractions, and architectural mastery. The sweeping panorama across the opposite Ahorn plateau and the glistening peaks along the Zillertal ridge creates an unforgettable mountain atmosphere. The distinctive landmark of the joch is the Granatkapelle (Garnet Chapel), consecrated in 2013 and designed by celebrated Swiss architect Mario Botta: The geometric structure resembles a faceted garnet crystal, honoring traditional Zillertal mineral stones while providing a serene, contemplative contrast to the vibrant outdoor landscape. Alongside the chapel, the Penken reservoir reflects surrounding limestone crags and invites quiet reflection.

Route & Requirements

Access infrastructure is world-class: From Mayrhofen, the cutting-edge 3S Penkenbahn glides to the upper station, where the Kombibahn Penken ascends directly to the summit ridge. Alternatively, the modern Finkenberger Almbahn carries visitors directly up from Finkenberg. From Penkenjoch, level, stroller-friendly paths lead around the reservoir and to the chapel (walking time approx. 15 minutes, very easy). Families find endless entertainment at the FunSportStation with mountain scooters, motor skills parcours, and interactive water elements. For hikers, the ridge is a launchpad to conquer the Wanglspitz (2,420 m) or embark on panoramic ridge hikes towards the Rastkogel (walking time approx. 3 hours, difficulty T2). Comfortable sneakers suffice on the plateau; sturdy hiking boots are required for alpine paths.

Visit & Arrival

Cable cars run continuously from late May until mid-October. The valley town of Mayrhofen is seamlessly connected via the Zillertalbahn railway from Jenbach, with trains arriving every half hour. The Penkenbahn valley terminal sits in central Mayrhofen, with parking provided. Holders of the Zillertal Activcard enjoy daily included cable car rides.

Tips

Step inside the Granatkapelle to experience the mesmerizing daylight cascading through the skylight onto handcrafted larch wood walls. Afterward, sample fresh Zillertaler Krapfen on the sun terraces of traditional mountain taverns with unobstructed views of glistening glaciers.
